summary: @yudzxml/baileys 7.4.2 — Baileys fork with unverified media-handling primitives
details: Package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. Static patterns fired on lib/Utils/messages-media.js citing co-occurrence of require('child_process'), require('os'), require('http')/require('https'), and POST/GET/fetch calls, together with the literal string https://mmg.whatsapp.net (WhatsApp's own media host used by Baileys for legitimate media upload/download). Media handling in Baileys legitimately combines HTTP fetches to WhatsApp's servers with child_process invocations of ffmpeg for thumbnail/audio transcoding, so the flagged co-occurrence matches the library's documented purpose. Traced-code corroboration is not available in the record, and the fork's own diffs against upstream Baileys have not been characterized, leaving unresolved ambiguity about whether the fork adds any covert action (e.g., using the installer's WhatsApp session for author benefit) beyond upstream behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
